ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding >25%, authorized signatories, and foreign principals against: (i) domestic Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and Magnitsky Act administered by Global Affairs Canada; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) UK HM Treasury and EU consolidated sanctions; (v) FATF and FINTRAC public advisories; (vi) PEP databases (FATF international PEP standard including family members and close associates). Screening to be repeated at minimum every 90 days and upon any material change in ownership, directorship, or funding source. All screening evidence, customer identification, and risk assessment records must be retained for 5 years after termination of the business relationship per PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements, and made available to FINTRAC upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca) administered by the Registrar of Companies, British Columbia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French words or Arabic numerals; names in other scripts require an approved transliteration into Latin characters. The corporate legal element must be one of: Limited, Limitée, Incorporated, Incorporée, Corporation, Corp., Inc., Ltd., or 'ULC' (Unlimited Liability Company) for this entity. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to any existing BC or extra-provincial registered name, not contain prohibited punctuation or special characters, and must end with the required legal element. Approval is based on the corporate name search and review under BCA s. 20-21 and the BC Name Requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, banking, trust (Financial Institutions Act regulated)
Insurance, assurance (BC Financial Services Authority licensing required)
Architect, engineer, lawyer, barrister, solicitor, notary, accountant (restricted professional designations)
Royal, crown, municipal, federal, provincial, government or derivatives implying official status
Exchange, clearinghouse, broker, dealer, funds adviser (securities regulator trigger)
Canada, British Columbia, Vancouver or geographic derivatives requiring express consent
Cooperative, credit union, savings, loan (regulated financial cooperative terms)
Global, international, group, corporation (permitted only in compliance with distinctive-name rules)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies under BCA ss. 23-24 within 30 days of the rejection notice, providing distinguishing elements, NUANS/CHIPS search results, and trademark registrations to rebut confusion; (2) concurrently file a new name reservation request with an alternate distinctive design on BC Registry Corporate Online; (3) appeal any registrar decision to the British Columbia Supreme Court by judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within 60 days of the registrar's final decision; and (4) where ministerial approval is engaged, submit the prior written consent from the responsible ministry attached to the name request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions: the registered office and records office must be located at a physical street address in British Columbia where documents may be served during usual business hours and where the corporate records and registers are maintained; a P.O. Box is prohibited. A virtual-office arrangement is contractually acceptable for the administrative ULC holding vehicle, but the commercial EOR staffing activity requires a designated employment records location in BC or at the licensed outsourcing entity, and the Canada Revenue Agency and the BC Employment Standards Branch may require immediate production of personnel and payroll files at an auditable physical address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 18-25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months for a non-resident, virtual-office ULC in the staffing/Employer of Record sector; risk rises to approximately 40% upon an employee complaint, payroll remittance discrepancy, or CRA payroll audit trigger; mitigated by maintaining a compliant registered office, an outsourced EOR license arrangement, and complete electronic and physical personnel record retention.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 — ss. 5 (incorporation), 10 (articles), 12 (filing), 16 (notice of articles), 25 (names), 47 (records office), 48 (records agent), 126 (first directors), 137 (share issuance), 188 (written resolutions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Citizen Services, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application comprising Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) and Form 2 (Notice of Articles) under s. 12 of the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a BC unlimited liability company; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine under s. 137 BCBCA. No statutory escrow account is required for the initial share subscription; subscription funds are held in the incorporating solicitor's pooled trust account pending issuance of shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, THAT the share subscription submitted by the incorporator — a subscription by the sole initial shareholder for 100 Class A common shares at CAD $10.00 per share — is accepted, and the Secretary is directed to issue the shares upon receipt of the aggregate subscription amount.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT the registered records office at [Registered Office Address], Vancouver, British Columbia, is adopted as the Corporation's registered office.

RESOLVED, FURTHER, THAT [Director Name] is appointed sole director, [Name] President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until successors are elected or appointed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Name Request Office (Corporate Online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search through a licensed BC Registry agent or the Corporate Online gateway; submit a Name Request (Form NR) listing three to five proposed corporate names, each containing the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or 'ULC'; the registrar reserves the approved name for 56 days; incorporation must be filed within that reservation window or the name reverts to availability.
required_dossiers: Consent to use distinctive words, if applicable
Statement of the proposed legal element (ULC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected under s. 25 BCBCA as confusing or prohibited, submit a Request for Reconsideration with written submissions to the Corporate Registry, or file a revised Form NR within the 56-day reservation period; registry review is completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitutional Documents (Articles and Notice of Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating legal counsel and BC Registries recognized software filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) under s. 10 BCBCA setting out the corporate name, the statement that the company is an unlimited liability company, the authorized share structure, special rights or restrictions, and the first directors; draft Form 2 (Notice of Articles) under s. 16 BCBCA stating the registered records office, records agent, directors, and share classes; execute both forms and obtain each first director's written consent.
required_dossiers: Unofficial NUANS report attached to the draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registrar issues a requisition listing deficiencies; rectify the articles or notice and resubmit within 30 days (s. 26 BCBCA); failure to cure the requisition abandons the filing and forfeits the statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into Corporate Online; upload the executed Form 1 and Form 2; pay the CAD $350 state filing fee by credit card or direct debit; upon successful system validation the Certificate of Incorporation, bearing the incorporation number, is issued immediately; for a ULC the certificate records the unlimited liability designation on the Notice of Articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal rejects the application, review the validation report, correct field-level errors (e.g., defective name elements or missing director consents), and resubmit; portal defects can also be cured telephonically through the Registry Solutions Desk (1-877-526-1526) on the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Records Office and Appointment of Records Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry, BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the records office is a physical street address in British Columbia and not a post-office box; appoint a records agent who is an individual ordinarily resident in BC or a corporation authorized to carry on business in BC (ss. 47-48 BCBCA); file the records office and records agent particulars as part of the Notice of Articles and retain the agent's written consent in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles containing the records office address
Written consent of the records agent
Proof of physical occupancy (lease or landlord confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the records agent withdraws consent, file Form 4 (Notice of Change of Registered Office and/or Records Agent) within 14 days to substitute a compliant agent; the registry processes the change to restore statutory compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (corporate governance record)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution under s. 188 BCBCA; approve the share subscription under s. 137 and authorize issuance of share certificates; adopt the registered records office under s. 47; appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer under s. 157; file the executed pro-forma resolution, share subscriptions, and consents in the corporate records book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a first director declines to sign the written resolution, convene a formally noticed meeting or obtain the sole shareholder's unanimous consent; defective appointments are ratified by a subsequent shareholder resolution under s. 137 BCBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online and BC Ministry of Finance (Employer Health Tax, WorkSafeBC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a CRA Business Number online; register the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and payroll deduction account (source deductions); register for the BC Employer Health Tax and obtain a WorkSafeBC account for office-based workers; apply for the municipal business licence at the physical office location; if supplying employees to BC users, file the Employment Agency Licence application with the Employment Standards Branch under s. 12 of the Employment Standards Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA verification mismatches are reconciled through the BRS Contact Centre; if an assessment or registration is disputed, relief may be requested under s. 220(3.1) of the Income Tax Act, and provincial registrations may be appealed to the Employment Standards Branch within the statutory review period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Employment Standards Branch, Ministry of Labour, Province of British Columbia; municipal business licensing authority for the physical office location
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employment Agency Licence (s. 12, Employment Standards Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 113) applicable to Global Employer of Record services supplying employee services to BC users, together with a Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Province of British Columbia
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Schedule B of the Reviewable Projects Regulation (B.C. Reg. 370/2002) does not list office-based EOR and payroll administration services; no full EIA certificate or environmental registration is required for a leased office footprint under 500 m²
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None directly applicable to payroll-only business operations; comply with BC Building Code Part 6 (indoor air quality and ventilation), municipal noise and wastewater bylaws, and the Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 449/2004) for e-waste disposal; any future warehouse or data-centre expansion must meet municipal air-shed emission thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection certificate and occupancy permit from the municipal fire marshal and building official under the Building Act (S.B.C. 2015, c. 6); WorkSafeBC employer registration and compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation (B.C. Reg. 296/1997) covering emergency evacuation plans, first-aid supplies, and ergonomic workstations; structural load inspection for high-density filing and IT server equipment

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation of banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distributions, or capital repatriation for a British Columbia unlimited liability corporation (BC ULC). Non-resident shareholders may freely repatriate funds after satisfying Canadian withholding tax requirements (e.g., Part XIII tax on dividends, branch tax where applicable) under the Income Tax Act and relevant tax treaties. The Investment Canada Act may impose notification or review obligations when non-residents acquire 'control' of a Canadian business, but this does not constrain convertibility. In practice, a ULC can hold foreign currency accounts with domestic banks and convert at a free-market rate without central bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law does not mandate the surrender, conversion, or repatriation of export proceeds within a statutory timeline. An employer of record (EOR) and staffing entity may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore bank accounts or convert them to Canadian dollars at a freely negotiated rate. Transactions above CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC as large cash or wire transfers, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and Statistics Canada may collect trade data for statistical purposes. No mandatory conversion ratio or holding period applies to export proceeds or cross-border service income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (including segregated Payroll Trust sub-account) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (including segregated Payroll Trust sub-account) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (with Global Money Transfer capabilities) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High viability as a complementary payment rail, but not as a substitute for a Schedule I bank account. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Payoneer, and Currencycloud must be registered as money services businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and hold the requisite provincial regulatory status (e.g., British Columbia's Money Lenders Act). The Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) imposes mandatory registration and operational risk management requirements. For a BC ULC engaged in global EOR payroll, licensed fintech EMIs can process low-value cross-border contractor payments efficiently, but the primary payroll, client trust balances, and capital escrow accounts must remain with a federally regulated Canadian bank to ensure legal protection under provincial employment standards and creditor claims in insolvency.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal or provincial statutory mandate requires directors to appear physically in a bank branch. FINTRAC's Client Identification Requirements permit electronic identity verification and remote onboarding. All six major Canadian Schedule I banks support remote video-based KYC interviews for Canadian-resident directors; non-resident directors may be required to provide notarized or apostilled passports, certified corporate resolutions, and pass a supplementary bank-specific risk assessment. In complex ownership structures involving a ULC's statutory flexibility (e.g., a non-resident shareholder), the bank's Privacy and Compliance Officer may require an escalated video interview or written legal opinion from Canadian counsel before approving the account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border disbursement patterns characteristic of an EOR platform, especially when paying contractors in multiple jurisdictions with varying AML maturity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Include BC Registrar corporate register extract, employment agency licence issued under the BC Employment Standards Act, detailed ownership org chart showing ultimate beneficial owners of the ULC, executed client master service agreement, template contractor engagement agreement, a three-month payroll funding projection, comprehensive AML/ATF internal compliance manual, written designation of the chief anti-money laundering officer, and a business rationale memorandum explaining the commercial need for each payment corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited liability structure may be flagged as a potential asset-shielding or tax-avoidance vehicle, particularly when a foreign parent owns the entity without a clear business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legal opinion from Canadian counsel on the ULC's pass-through tax classification under the Income Tax Act (and BC provincial mirror legislation), the shareholder indemnity agreement, audited or reviewed financial statements, evidence of substantive business activity (e.g., payroll runs, employment contracts, HR systems), and a declaration that the ULC is not used for asset stripping or as a shell. Confirm the entity is 'resident in Canada' under paragraph 250(4)(b) of the Income Tax Act and has no disqualifying international tax avoidance motive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual electronic funds transfer alerts from the bank's transaction monitoring system due to rapid layering through multiple EMI or fintech wallets, perceived as potential money laundering or unauthorized money transmission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a transaction-mapping report for all clearing rails, segregating client payroll trust transactions from corporate operating expenses; a monthly reconciliation statement of payroll liabilities vs. disbursed amounts; a reseller or white-label agreement (if any) proving the ULC is not operating as an unlicensed money transmitter; a sworn statutory declaration from the CEO detailing the organic commercial purpose of each cross-border transfer; and an audit trail showing that all funds emanate from identified client accounts and are paid to identified ultimate beneficiaries (contractors).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or debt injections into the BC ULC must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or SWIFT MT202 according to the sending and intermediary bank requirements. The remitter field (50K) must disclose the actual shareholder or lender, the beneficiary field (59) must show the ULC's trust or operational account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, and the remittance information field (70) must contain a clear purpose code, such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION TO CANADA ULC' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN TO CANADA ULC'. The ULC must provide the bank with a certified copy of the board resolution authorizing the capital injection and a completed source of funds declaration for the beneficial owner. All inbound wires exceeding CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC large transaction reporting; the bank will verify the transaction against the Investment Canada Act thresholds and, if control is acquired, the non-resident shareholder may need to file a notification with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for disbursing contractor wages and trade settlements is SWIFT MT103, sent directly from the ULC's Canadian corporate banking portal to beneficiary bank accounts worldwide. For large trade payables (e.g., subcontracting or licencing fees), a documentary letter of credit (Commercial LC) can be used through the ULC's bank, although open account transfers are the prevailing industry practice. For high-volume, low-value contractor payroll, the ULC may integrate a fintech EMI such as Wise using batch-transfer APIs, provided the EMI is FINTRAC-registered and the transfers are mirrored in the ULC's payroll ledger. The bank may require pre-funding of payroll in segregated client trust accounts to mitigate operational risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (under ISDA Canadian Master Agreement or bank's standard FX terms)
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed or floating variation, with optional principal exchange)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted, non-convertible emerging-market currencies
FX Options (European-style, OTC, pristine or covered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined BC general rate 27.0% (Federal 15% + BC provincial 12%); small business rate 11.0% (Federal 9% + BC provincial 2%) on first C$500,000 active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: BC Small Business Deduction with C$500,000 business limit; Federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credit 35% (25% non-refundable for CCPCs beyond limits); BC SR&ED provincial credit 10% up to C$250,000; Manufacturing and processing federal rate reduction; clean-technology investment tax credits; dividend refund mechanism through RDTOH for portfolio dividends

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) with integrated BC provincial schedules (T2BC); filed electronically via CRA EFILE or certified third-party software; accessed through CRA 'My Business Account'; form T106 (Transfer Pricing Disclosure) attached as part of Schedule 88
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal period return (maximum 53 weeks); interim instalment payments monthly or quarterly based on prior-year taxes and estimated current-year taxable income
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months of fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after fiscal year-end, extended to 3 months for eligible CCPCs claiming the Small Business Deduction under s. 157(3) ITA; non-resident corporations carrying on business in BC through a permanent establishment file on the same timetable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name, Business Number (BN), incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal period end, business activity code (NAICS 561330), mailing address and authorized contact
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident ownership percentages in Schedule 3 and identify country of the foreign parent; a non-resident corporation carrying on business in BC must include its Canadian PE income attribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residency status, Small Business Deduction business limit allocation, controlled foreign affiliate status, passive income vs active business income classification, substantiating the EOR operational activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A BC-incorporated ULC is deemed resident in Canada under s. 250(5) ITA regardless of central management and control; choose 'resident' and attach treaty disclosure if dual-residency or treaty-shopping risk is identified

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: EOR administrative margins and contractor bond fees less payroll costs, licensing fees, software subscriptions, benefits, rent, legal, banking and transfer-pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges from the foreign EOR parent to the BC ULC must be arm's-length under s. 247(2) and disclosed on Form T106; inflated management or IP royalties are non-deductible to the extent inconsistent with the arm's-length range

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 308 and 310 – Federal basic tax and abatement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic federal rate 28% reduced by 10% provincial abatement to 15% general, or 9% on income eligible for the Small Business Deduction; additional 5% surtax may apply for non-resident-owned investment corporations (NROIC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Active EOR service revenue avoids NROIC characterization; the US parent must avoid causing the ULC to hold predominantly passive financial assets without an active staffing operation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 331 / 420 – Total federal tax and total taxes payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net federal tax after all credits combined with BC T2BC tax calculation and foreign tax credits; includes the BC general 12% rate or BC small business 2% rate on eligible income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: BC PE income allocation uses Schedule T2BC 5 (Table 5 – BC allocation); a non-resident corporation failing to complete BC provincial schedules will not receive the benefit of the BC small business rate and may be assessed under federal Part I at full provincial surcharge rates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 4 – Line 606 – Dividend Refund / RDTOH accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of refundable dividend tax on hand (RDTOH) and dividend refunds flowing from EOR retained earnings; preserves integration for Canadian-resident shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any dividend declared to the US parent triggers Part XIII NR4 withholding at 25% unless a treaty-based waiver is filed on Form NR301; reduced treaty rates require beneficial ownership and cannot be claimed through a bare ULC without economic substance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeat failure penalty escalates to 10%; late or deficient instalments attract prescribed interest compounded daily; failure to file T106 transfer-pricing schedules carries penalties of C$2,500 per month for each complete month up to 24 months; NR4 information returns are subject to C$25 to C$2,500 per form and an additional penalty for deliberate omission

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to non-resident shareholders under s. 212(2) ITA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For Canada–US DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner submits Form NR301 (Treaty-Based Withholding Waiver) to the withholding agent, or applies to the CRA for a treaty-resident exemption; the payer must verify beneficial ownership and review a valid US IRS Form 6166 Certificate of Residence; on approval the payer withholds at the treaty rate of 5% (corporate shareholder owning 10% or more of voting stock) or 15% for portfolio shareholders; CRA may request evidence of economic substance before granting the reduced rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory Part XIII rate 25%; Canada–US treaty rate 0% for arm's-length interest, 10% for non-arm's-length interest. Royalties: statutory Part XIII rate 25%; Canada–US treaty rate 10% generally, 0% for qualifying cultural copyright royalties and certain computer software royalties; industrial royalties, patents and know-how remain at 10%. Treaty benefits require TRC or equivalent proof of US residence and beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: C$1,000,000 aggregate non-arm's-length cross-border transactions; Master File: C$10,000,000 aggregate threshold; Country-by-Country Report: consolidated group revenue of C$900,000,000 or more
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code, but incorporates economic-substance analysis through the GAAR in s. 245 ITA, the treaty abuse rule in the MLI (Article 29(9) applying to the Canada–US treaty), and PE attribution rules in s. 253 ITA / Article V. The BC ULC must demonstrate genuine employment contracts, payroll processing capabilities, local staffing personnel, and strategic control over its EOR activities. A ULC functioning as a mere invoicing conduit without real personnel or payroll infrastructure will fail treaty relief, lose the Small Business Deduction, and be reassessed as a shell with a PE of the foreign parent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Statements (s. 163(2), s. 238 and s. 239 ITA)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a false T2 return, omitting EOR payroll revenue, fabricating intercompany management fees, backdating staffing contracts, or knowingly understating taxable income to shift profit to the US parent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of understated tax plus prescribed interest; on criminal conviction, a fine equal to 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 5 years (summary conviction) or up to 14 years (indictment)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or acquiesce to false filings are personally chargeable under s. 239(1); the CRA may impose travel restrictions and passport surrender pending prosecution; the court can order restitution of evaded taxes; under BC Business Corporations Act the shareholders of a ULC remain personally liable for corporate civil tax debts, effectively piercing the corporate veil

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Source Deductions / Part XIII WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold and remit Canadian source deductions (CPP, EI, income tax) from EOR employees, or failing to remit Part XIII withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-resident shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unremitted amounts become immediately due; CRA discretion to apply seal or quarterly penalties; 10% failure-to-remit penalty on amounts not remitted within prescribed time; interest at the CRA prescribed rate compounded daily
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s. 227.1 ITA, directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and Part XIII amounts regardless of delegation; liability survives corporate insolvency and dissolution; CRA may file a certificate and obtain a provincial court enforcement order, trigger banking garnishments, and freeze director travel pending criminal examination

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping / Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a BC ULC with no employees, payroll platforms, physical office, or client contracts, solely to convert US-source staffing revenues into Canadian dividends or to claim treaty-reduced WHT while the foreign parent performs all EOR functions outside Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment under s. 245 ITA removes the treaty or Small Business Deduction benefit; s. 163.2 misrepresentation penalty applies up to C$100,000 and 50% of the tax benefit for gross negligence; the ULC profits are recharacterized as a PE profit of the foreign parent and assessed under Part XIV branch tax at 25%; treaty relief is denied retroactively with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving a sham structure are exposed to breach of fiduciary duty claims and civil actions by the CRA for corporate strip-downs; where assets were upstreamed to shareholders before reassessment, courts have disregarded the ULC limitation structure and imposed restitution obligations on senior officers; travel bans and asset freezes may be ordered pending fraud or GAAR litigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed EOR / Employment Agency in BC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing global EOR, worker recruitment, placement, or payroll contracting services in BC under ISIC 7810 without the mandatory licence under the BC Employment Standards Act and Employment and Labour Relations Regulations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to C$5,000 per contravention; director orders to stop operating; adjudication orders for unpaid wages and statutory entitlements; retroactive CPP/EI/income-tax reassessments for misclassified independent contractors within the previous three years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: BC directors and officers may be personally fined for contraventions where the corporation is ordered to pay wages to EOR employees; failure to pay accrued wages constitutes criminal fraud under s. 380(1) Criminal Code; because the entity is a ULC, shareholders bear unlimited personal liability for wage claims and employment standards payments

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing cross-border EOR payroll through Wise or alternate payment rails without registering with FINTRAC as a money services business, failing to file large virtual currency transaction reports, or operating without an AML compliance program and designated compliance officer
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalty up to C$1,200,000 for an individual and C$10,000,000 for an entity for each violation; FINTRAC may suspend or terminate the business relationship; criminal prosecution under the PCMLTFA for knowingly attempting to evade registration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly fail to prevent money-laundering practices face criminal liability with fines up to C$10,000,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years; the BC Prosecution Service may impose restrictions on leaving Canada upon charging; corporate registration and reputation loss multiplies personal civil exposure to affected EOR clients and employees
